title: M-Pesa and Mobile Money: How East Africa Moved $806 Billion in 2025 | The Six, Ep. 4
lede: East Africa moved $806 billion through mobile money in 2025, more than half of sub-Saharan Africa's total. This episode traces how M-Pesa launched in Kenya on a central bank's letter of no objection, how big it has become, who owns it, and the new payments bill that would rewrite the rules.
keyPoints: Mobile money transactions in East Africa reached $806 billion in 2025, out of $1.4 trillion in sub-Saharan Africa and more than $2 trillion worldwide (GSMA, March 2026).
Kenya had about 54 million active mobile money subscriptions in June 2026; M-Pesa held 88.8% and Airtel Money 11.1% (Communications Authority of Kenya).

In the year to March 2026, M-Pesa handled 46.4 billion transactions worth KES 41.7 trillion (about US$322 billion) and earned KES 182.7 billion, 45.6% of Safaricom Kenya's service revenue. Fuliza lent KES 1.47 trillion.
Vodacom completed the purchase of the Kenyan government's 15% Safaricom stake on June 30, 2026, taking its holding to 55%; the state kept 20%.
Kenya's draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 would let the central bank order interoperability, require consent-based data sharing and appoint statutory managers. Comments closed Oct. 9.
